content: The following references provide detailed insights into various aspects of hepatitis B and C management, prevention, and treatment strategies: 1. Chronic hepatitis B coexisting with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease presents unique challenges and opportunities for management, as discussed by Chun-Jen Liu in Clinical and Molecular Hepatology (2023). 2. Huang et al. explored the use of fatty liver progression inhibition algorithms and steatosis, activity, and fibrosis scores to evaluate the impact of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease on untreated chronic hepatitis B patients in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology (2022). 3. 4. Musabaev et al. highlighted the challenges of viral hepatitis elimination in lowand middle-income countries, focusing on the Uzbekistan Hepatitis Elimination Programme in Liver International (2023). 5. Guidelines for the prevention, care, and treatment of chronic hepatitis B infection were outlined by the WHO, emphasizing evidence-based approaches (2024). 6. Wang et al. demonstrated that primary non-response to antiviral therapy significantly impacts the prognosis of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma in BMC Cancer (2023). 7. Lin et al. developed a predictive model for hepatocellular carcinoma risk in chronic hepatitis B patients undergoing finite antiviral therapy in Cancers (2023). 8. Lee et al. evaluated the clinical effects of antiviral therapy in patients with hepatitis B virus-related decompensated cirrhosis and undetectable DNA levels in Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology (2023). 9. Kim and Ahn proposed a prediction model for hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma in patients receiving antiviral therapy in Journal of the Formosan Medical Association (2023). 10. Rasool et al. investigated the frequency of de novo hepatocellular carcinoma following direct-acting antiviral therapy for chronic hepatitis C in Euroasian Journal of Hepatogastroenterology (2022). 11. Lee et al. developed a long-term prediction model for hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis B patients receiving antiviral therapy, based on data from Korean patients in Journal of Clinical Medicine (2022). 12. Chang et al. identified HBcrAg as a predictor of hepatocellular carcinoma development in chronic hepatitis B-related cirrhosis patients undergoing long-term effective antiviral therapy in Viruses (2022). 13. Wong et al. conducted a cohort study on the long-term safety of oral nucleos(t)ide analogs in chronic hepatitis B patients, involving over 53,500 subjects, published in Hepatology (2015). 14. Marcellin et al. reported on the regression of cirrhosis during treatment with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for chronic hepatitis B in a 5-year open-label follow-up study in The Lancet (2013). 15. Oh et al. demonstrated improved on-treatment fibrosis-4 scores and reduced hepatocellular carcinoma risk in cirrhotic hepatitis B patients receiving antiviral therapy in Scientific Reports (2023). 16. Huang et al. showed that antiviral therapy significantly reduces hepatocellular carcinoma risk in chronic hepatitis B patients in the indeterminate phase in Hepatology (2023). 17. Hu et al. analyzed the effectiveness of antiviral treatment in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B patients with ALT levels below twice the upper limit of normal in a multicenter retrospective cohort study in Infectious Diseases and Therapy (2023). 18. Cheng et al. investigated the reversibility of oxidative stress markers in chronic hepatitis C patients after direct-acting antiviral therapy in Journal of Virus Eradication (2023). 19. Hsu et al. examined the determinants of functional cure during entecavir or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate therapy for chronic hepatitis B in Journal of Infectious Diseases (2021). 20. Yip et al. found that HBsAg seroclearance further reduces hepatocellular carcinoma risk after complete viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogs in Journal of Hepatology (2019). 21. Lim et al. provided evidence supporting the benefits of early treatment initiation for chronic hepatitis B in Viruses (2023). 22. Huang et al. conducted a network meta-analysis comparing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma in antiviral-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients treated with entecavir or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in BMC Cancer (2022). 23. Wong et al. performed a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials on antiviral treatment for treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis B in Systematic Reviews (2019). 24. Wang et al. compared the effects of tenofovir and entecavir on the prognosis of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma after curative resection in Journal of Gastroenterology (2022). 25. Chen et al. evaluated the impact of direct-acting antiviral therapy on recurrence risk after curative resection in hepatitis C virus-related early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma in Medicina (2022). 26. Yuan et al. conducted a meta-analysis showing a lower risk of hepatocellular carcinoma with tenofovir compared to entecavir in chronic hepatitis B patients in Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology (2022). 27. Kim et al. assessed the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma in treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate versus entecavir in the United States in Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics (2022). 28. Choi et al. discussed methodological challenges in performing meta-analyses comparing hepatocellular carcinoma risk between chronic hepatitis B treatments in Journal of Hepatology (2022). 29. Lampertico et al. conducted a randomized, double-blind, phase 3 study on switching from tenofovir disoproxil fumarate to tenofovir alafenamide in virologically suppressed chronic hepatitis B patients in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology (2020). 30. Byun et al. evaluated tenofovir alafenamide for drug-resistant hepatitis B in a randomized trial for switching from tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. 31. Pilkington et al. performed a meta-analysis comparing tenofovir alafenamide and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in 14,894 patients across 14 trials in AIDS (2020). 32. Schwarz et al. reported no detected resistance to tenofovir alafenamide in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B in a week 24 primary endpoint analysis by Gilead Sciences (2019). 33. Sax et al. compared tenofovir alafenamide and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in single-tablet regimens for initial HIV-1 therapy in a randomized phase 2 study in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (2014). 34. Kauppinen et al. found that switching from tenofovir alafenamide to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate improves lipid profiles and prevents weight gain in AIDS (2022). 35. Milinkovic et al. demonstrated reversible lipid effects when switching between tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and tenofovir alafenamide in AIDS (2019). 36. Chen et al. assessed the safety and efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide in early-mid pregnancy for mothers with chronic hepatitis B in Frontiers in Medicine (2021). 37. Lockman et al. evaluated dolutegravir-based regimens with tenofovir alafenamide or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in pregnant women in a phase 3 trial in The Lancet (2021). 38. Schwarz et al. presented findings on the safety and efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B at the EASL International Liver Congress (2022). 39. The WHO consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and monitoring provide a public health approach to managing viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (2021). 40. Shimakawa et al. studied the residual risk of mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission despite timely birth-dose vaccination in Cameroon in The Lancet Global Health (2022). 41. Funk et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy and safety of antiviral prophylaxis during pregnancy to prevent hepatitis B transmission in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (2021). 42. Thompson et al. explored the feasibility of preventing vertical hepatitis B transmission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in The Lancet Global Health (2021). 43. Nachega et al. reviewed the safety of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-based antiretroviral therapy in pregnancy for HIV-infected women and their infants in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (2017). 44. Ding and Dou discussed serum HBV RNA biphasic decline in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B patients treated with nucleos(t)ide analogs in Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics (2020). 45. Ehrhardt et al. reviewed breastfeeding safety while taking lamivudine or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in Clinical Infectious Diseases (2015). 46. Liotta et al. compared growth indices in breastfed infants exposed to tenofovir prenatally versus unexposed infants in AIDS (2016). 47. Nayagam et al. modeled the impact and cost-effectiveness of hepatitis B prophylaxis in pregnancy in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology (2023). 48. Segeral et al. evaluated an immunoglobulin-free strategy to prevent HBV mother-to-child transmission in Cambodia in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (2022). 49. Yao et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the incidence of mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission in relation to maternal peripartum antiviral prophylaxis in Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica (2022). 50. Nayagam et al. outlined the requirements for global hepatitis B elimination in a modeling study in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (2016).
